diagnostic: AntMaze V6: task-goal target support per candidate action on the stage-1 query futures, current vs absorbing termination law (no rollouts, no training)

laws.current: P(m) ~ gamma^m over m = 1..L-1 (CriticStream.draw; each path normalised over its own rows)
laws.absorbing: P(m) ~ gamma^m over m = 1..H, H = HORIZON - t; rows m >= L-1 of a success / death branch are the branch's actual terminal row; a timeout (L-1 == H) is unchanged.  No relabelling: no death filled in as a goal, no reach position replaced by the goal centre, success and death both get the tail

marginal: anchor-weighted mean of the per-anchor law over ALL 53,747 anchors: the CF sealed branch table (what the lineage critics trained on) and the recorded futures (arm O); the law of the NCE negatives
weights: anchor weight (the critic anchor law); unweighted (per-anchor equal) in report.json
route_classes: a query is far-going if its future entered the far route in BOTH draws, short-going if in neither; mixed queries are excluded from R4 and their share reported

read_outs.R1: per query: success, far completion, death, timeout, expected task-goal mass under both laws
read_outs.R2: within (anchor, draw) pairs of queries with different outcome classes: P(mass_good > mass_bad), mean difference, ratio of means
read_outs.R3: per anchor: concordance across the six queries between the success rate (two draws) and the expected mass; top-1 agreement
read_outs.R4: per anchor with both route classes: delta success (far - short) vs delta expected task-goal mass under both laws; paired-by-anchor bootstrap; sign agreement (PRIMARY)

judgement.J1_current_weakens_or_reverses: in the reset stratum, reach_0.5: far-going queries succeed more (delta_success mean > 0, CI lower bound > 0) while under the CURRENT law delta_mass is not above zero (CI covers 0 or lies below) OR p_sign_agree_given_far_better < 0.5
judgement.J2_absorbing_improves: under the ABSORBING law delta_mass mean > 0 with CI lower bound > 0 AND p_sign_agree_given_far_better above the current law's

decision.J1 and J2 in every lineage: the user's option 1: a small O / CF mainline comparison with the same termination handling in both arms (NCE, BC 0.05, actor data, weights, budget unchanged; disclosed as a changed future law) -- the user's call
decision.otherwise: the user's option 2: the termination rule is not a found cause; the problem stays in how the learner / policy update uses the target; stop this hypothesis

judgement.secondary: R3 concordance and top-1 agreement (both laws); R2 far_success vs short_success (the pure speed penalty) -- reported, not part of the rule
